synopsis: Sobol sequences are space-filling, quasi-random designs that spread simulation runs evenly through a chosen parameter region; the glossary compares their spread with Latin hypercube designs while noting that they work differently [f14137, f14843, f7228]. Chapter 9 says these schemes cover continuous parameters more evenly than naive random draws and recommends them for continuous-space coverage, surrogate training and broad exploration [f6813, f6814, f7227]. This geometric coverage does not establish unweighted rates, worst cases or operational frequency, and unrealistic regions receive equal treatment unless constraints and distributions are added [f7229, f7230]. Typical implementation uses open-source libraries and in-house tools, but the stated evidence base is generic expert opinion from statistical synthesis rather than program-specific validation evidence [f7231, f7232].
